24/7 Clinics Achieve UCA Accreditation in Chicago: A Milestone for Global Urgent Care
Chicago, USA, 24/7 Clinics becomes the first urgent care organization outside the United States accredited by the Urgent Care Association, marking a major milestone in global healthcare standards.

24/7 Clinics, part of Healthcare International Group (HCIG), has reached a defining milestone in its international development, becoming the first urgent care organization outside the United States to be accredited by the Urgent Care Association (UCA) through the Commission on Ambulatory and Urgent Care Quality (CAUCQ).

The accreditation was formally recognized in Chicago, placing 24/7 Clinics among a highly selective group of providers operating under globally recognized urgent care standards, standards originally developed within one of the most advanced and structured healthcare systems in the world.

This achievement reflects more than compliance. It confirms that a model built and operated internationally can meet the same level of clinical discipline, operational consistency, and system accountability expected within the United States.

At the core of this recognition is the way 24/7 Clinics has been designed from the beginning. Rather than functioning as standalone medical points, the network operates as part of an integrated system developed by HCIG, one that is built to perform in real-world conditions where urgency, complexity, and coordination define outcomes.

Within this model, urgent care is not limited to immediate treatment. It is structured as a complete pathway that includes triage, clinical decision-making, escalation when required, and direct coordination with hospitals, insurance companies, and assistance providers. Each stage follows clearly defined protocols aligned with international standards.

This is precisely what UCA accreditation evaluates. It does not focus solely on facilities or individual clinical expertise, but on whether healthcare delivery is consistent, whether patient safety is embedded in operations, and whether systems can sustain performance under pressure.

For 24/7 Clinics, this validation is particularly significant within the context of travel medicine. Unlike traditional healthcare environments, international patient care operates across unfamiliar systems, limited timeframes, and multiple stakeholders. In such conditions, the absence of structure often leads to delays, miscommunication, and fragmented care.

By aligning with UCA standards, 24/7 Clinics addresses this challenge directly. It creates a controlled and predictable environment where patient journeys are managed with clarity, speed, and accountability, from the first point of contact through to resolution.

This approach strengthens the role of 24/7 Clinics within the global travel medical ecosystem. For insurance companies and assistance providers, it ensures that clinical and operational processes follow a consistent framework. For hospitality partners, it provides reliable on-site urgent care that integrates seamlessly into the guest experience. And for patients, it delivers something that is often missing in cross-border healthcare, confidence.
The recognition in Chicago marks a moment where this model is not only implemented, but independently validated.

It also contributes to a broader shift in how international healthcare is perceived. As markets like Egypt continue to evolve within medical tourism, the ability to demonstrate globally recognized standards becomes essential, not only in clinical capability, but in system performance.
For 24/7 Clinics, this milestone reflects the work of teams across the entire network, consistently operating under demanding conditions and maintaining alignment with international protocols.
Because in urgent care, outcomes are not defined by intention, but by execution.
The accreditation achieved in Chicago confirms that 24/7 Clinics delivers both.
Strengthening Egypt’s Healthcare Presence on the Global Stage

Cairo, Egypt, Strengthening Egypt’s position on the global healthcare and medical tourism map begins with real partnerships, open dialogue, and a clear understanding of what international readiness truly means.

Strengthening Egypt’s position on the global healthcare and medical tourism map begins with real partnerships, open dialogue, and a clear understanding of what international readiness truly means. Healthcare International Group (HCIG), together with Bonnie Zdraveva, RN, Regional Accreditation Lead at Global Healthcare Accreditation (GHA), recently conducted a series of site visits to leading hospitals in Cairo, including El Safa Hospital, AlMehwar Hospital, Shifa Hospitals Group, and As-Salam International Hospital. These visits were not symbolic. They were focused, practical, and aimed at evaluating readiness for international patient services while engaging hospital leadership in meaningful conversations about quality standards, patient experience, and global expectations.

Medical tourism today is no longer defined only by clinical outcomes or modern infrastructure. International patients, insurance companies, and global partners increasingly assess hospitals through trust, transparency, cultural competence, and the ability to operate within internationally recognized frameworks. A hospital can be well equipped, technologically advanced, and beautifully designed, yet still not fully prepared to serve international patients. Global readiness requires structured systems, trained teams, consistent patient experience, and alignment with international standards.

During the visits, HCIG and GHA explored hospital infrastructure, reviewed operational capabilities, and discussed how international accreditation supports healthcare providers in moving beyond local markets. Conversations focused on how hospitals can responsibly increase the flow of medical tourists, improve service quality, strengthen operational processes, and meet the expectations of international insurers and assistance companies. Particular attention was given to the importance of cultural competence, communication, and patient-centered care for travelers seeking treatment abroad.

Global Healthcare Accreditation is not about labels or certificates displayed on walls. It represents systematic transformation. GHA supports hospitals in building credibility with international partners, standardizing patient experience, improving internal processes, and preparing teams to confidently deliver care to international patients. Accreditation is not an end goal; it is a pathway to trust, consistency, and long-term global growth.

As the official GHA Partner in Egypt, Healthcare International Group continues to support hospitals throughout this journey, from initial assessment and readiness to international positioning and market integration. HCIG’s role goes beyond evaluation. It includes strategic guidance, operational alignment, and long-term partnership building to help Egyptian healthcare providers compete confidently within the global medical tourism ecosystem.

We extend our sincere appreciation to the hospital leaders and teams who welcomed us with openness and professionalism, including Dr. Sherif Hamdy, Business Development Manager at El Safa Hospital; Dr. Ayman Moharam, CEO of AlMehwar Hospital; Dr. Ahmed Magdi; Mr. Fathy Hashem of Shifa Hospitals Group; and Dr. Fahad Khater of As-Salam International Hospital. Their commitment to quality, transparency, and continuous improvement reflects the direction in which Egypt’s healthcare sector is moving.

As Egypt continues to strengthen its presence on the global stage, one message remains clear: real progress is built through standards, training, cultural competence, and trusted partnerships. Healthcare International Group, together with Global Healthcare Accreditation, remains committed to supporting hospitals across Egypt as they advance toward international readiness and sustainable growth in medical tourism.
